                                JUDGMENT
1. The present common judgment shall determine the aforenoted criminal appeal, bearing; Crl.
Appeal No. 427/2024, filed by the appellant, namely, E.S. Vasudevan ( hereinafter referred to as the
'accused/appellant') in terms of the provisions under Section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 (hereinafter, referred to as 'Cr.P.C./Code')/pari materia with Section 415 of Bharatiya Nagarik
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (hereinafter referred to as 'BNSS') and the criminal revision petition,
bearing; Crl. Rev. No. 516/2024, filed by/on behalf of the revisionist, Smt. Ved Kumari, acting
through her legal heir/husband, namely, Sh. Kewal Kishan Sethi (hereinafter referred to as the
'complainant/revisionist'), in terms of the provisions under Sections 397/399 Cr.P.C./pari materia
with Sections 438/440 BNSS. At the outset, it is noted that both the said proceedings emanate out of
judgment dated 06.05.2024 (hereinafter referred to as 'impugned judgment'), passed by learned
Metropolitan Magistrate (NI Act)-04/Ld. MM (NI Act)-04, Central, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi
(hereinafter referred to as the 'Ld. Trial Court/Ld. MM') in case bearing, 'Smt. Ved Kumari v. Sh.
E.S. Vasudevan, Ct. Case No. 7156/2018', in a complaint under Section 200 Cr.P.C. read with
Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (hereinafter referred to as 'NI Act'), convicting
the appellant/accused for the offence under Section 138 NI Act, and the consequent order of
sentence dated 13.09.2024 CA No. 427/2024 ES Vasudevan v. Ved Kumari, through SPA Holder CR
No. 516/2024 Ved Kumari through LR v. ES Vasudevan Page No. 2 of 51 ABHISHEK GOYAL

which, the accused was directed to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 03
(three) months and 15 (fifteen) days. However, under the impugned order, the
accused was conferred with the benefit of probation (hereinafter impugned judgment
and impugned order are collectively referred to as the 'impugned judgment and
order'). Pertinent to further note here that though, the accused has sought for setting
aside of the impugned judgment and order/order of sentence, however, the
complainant/revisionist has sought for enhancement of the sentence, awarded to the
accused by the Ld. Trial Court.

complainant before the Ld. Trial Court in terms of the provisions under Section 200 Cr.P.C. read
with Section 138 of NI Act, acting through her Special Power of Attorney Holder, Sh. Kewal Kishan
Sethi (hereinafter referred to as the 'SPA Holder/LR of complainant'). Pertinently, under the said
complaint, the complainant inter alia asserted that the complainant and the accused were
acquainted and in good friendly relationship with each other. As per the complainant, the accused

last week of August 2017, the accused approached her, requesting for a friendly loan to a tune of Rs.
3,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs only), expressing personal need, whilst assuring the complainant
that the said amount would be returned till December CA No. 427/2024 ES Vasudevan v. Ved

per the complainant, being wary of their past relationship and in order to maintain accused's
goodwill, the complainant is avowed to have arranged a said sum of Rs. 3,00,000/- (Rupees Three
Lakhs only) from her husband and loaned the same to the accused in three parts, i.e., a sum of Rs.
1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) in cash on 24.08.2017; Rs. 1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only)
in cash on 07.09.2017; and Rs. 1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) in cash on 12.09.2017. 2.1.
Markedly, it is further chronicled under the complainant's complaint that in the last week of
December 2017, when the complainant asked the accused to return the aforesaid loan amount, the
accused in discharge of his debt/liability, issued a cheque bearing no. 913451, dated 11.01.2018 for a
sum of Rs. 3,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs only), drawn on State Bank of India, Pratap Nagar
branch (hereinafter referred to as the 'cheque in question/dishonoured cheque'), in favour of the
complainant, with an assurance that the said cheque would be honoured on its presentation.
Consequently, the complainant is asserted to have presented the said cheque for its encashment
with its banker, State Bank of India, Pratap Nagar branch. However, the same was returned
dishonoured on 12.01.2018, under the remarks, 'Funds Insufficient'. Thereafter, the complainant is
stated to have contacted the accused, seeking explanation on dishonour of cheque. However, while
tendering different kinds of excuses, the accused is proclaimed to have asked to the complainant to
present the cheque for its encashment in the second week of February 2018. Accordingly, based on
the reassurances of the accused, the complainant is avowed to have again presented the cheque in
question for its encashment with its banker, i.e., State Bank of India, Pratap Nagar branch.
However, the same was again returned CA No. 427/2024 ES Vasudevan v. Ved Kumari, through

liability. Ergo, under such circumstances, the complainant filed the aforenoted
complaint in terms of the provisions under Section 138 NI Act before the Ld. Trial
Court.

"...Vide this order, I shall dispose off the application filed by the accused under
section 311 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for summoning the complainant,
Smt. Ved Kumari.
*** *** *** Arguments heard. Record perused.
It is pertinent to note that the accused has not disclosed any specific reason to call the
complainant. Further, the only stand taken by the accused is that he does not know
the complainant and that his cheques have been misplaced so no question of bringing
the complainant on record. The accused had to prove bis defence which was taken by
him that his cheques had been misplaced. The Ld. Counsel for the accused has failed
to put the specific questions which only the complainant can answer and not SPA
holder of the complainant. Also, the judgment of Janki Vashdeo Bhojwani & Anr. v.
Indusind Bank Ltd. & Ors. (supra) relied upon by the Ld. counsel for the accused as
the same was with respect to a civil suit and not with respect to the case under section
138 of the NI Act. It is also worthy to note that section 138 r/w section 145 of the NI
Act and the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of A.C. Narayanan v. State of
Maharashtra (supra), enables the cross- examination of the POA holder being a
technical and document-based offence and since the accused himself claims to not
know the complainant as alleged, thus there is no need to press for the presence of
the complainant who is herself a senior citizen. Further, the SPA holder has clearly
stated that in his power of attorney that being husband of the complainant, SPA
holder is well conversant about the friendly loan being advanced by the complainant
to the accused. The contention of the Ld. Counsel for the accused that the complete
details have not been mentioned regarding the witnesses does not hold good as the
witness are merely for identify the genuineness of the document and not for its
contents and will have no bearing on the genuineness of the document.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, the application filed by the accused under section
311 CrPC accordingly stands disposed off as dismissed..."
